# Data Preparation

## Part 1 — Data Source

I used daily weather records from NOAA Seattle Sand Point (`USW00094290`).
The requested period is January 1, 2015 through December 31, 2025.
The CSV was requested in metric units.

This is a single-station weather dataset, not a dataset of observed flooding.

## Part 2 — Load the Data

```{python}
import pandas as pd

weather_raw = pd.read_csv(
    "Data/Raw/seattle_sand_point_2015_2025.csv"
)

weather_raw.head()
```

```{python}
study_start = pd.Timestamp(
    "2015-01-01"
)

study_end = pd.Timestamp(
    "2025-12-31"
)

raw_dates = pd.to_datetime(
    weather_raw["DATE"],
    format="%Y-%m-%d"
)

if raw_dates.isna().any():
    raise ValueError(
        "A date is missing. Review the source file."
    )

full_date_range = pd.date_range(
    study_start,
    study_end,
    freq="D"
)

missing_dates = (
    full_date_range.difference(
        raw_dates
    )
)

print(
    "Missing dates:",
    len(
        missing_dates
    )
)

missing_dates
```

### 3.12 Inspection Findings

The source contains 3,989 records and no duplicate rows or station-date keys.

Two recorded dates have missing precipitation values.

Another 29 dates, June 1–29, 2023, are absent from the file entirely.

Missing rainfall is not zero rainfall. The file does not establish why
these observations are missing.

## Part 4 — Data Cleaning

`weather_raw` is the original in-memory table.

`weather` is a separate working copy.

Neither the raw table nor the source CSV is overwritten.

### 4.1 Create a Working Copy

```{python}
weather = weather_raw.copy()
```

### 4.2 Convert Date to Datetime

```{python}
weather[
    "DATE"
] = raw_dates

weather[
    "DATE"
].dtype
```

### 4.3 Validate the Station-Date Structure

```{python}
if weather[
    "STATION"
].isna().any():
    raise ValueError(
        "A station ID is missing."
    )

if weather[
    "STATION"
].nunique() != 1:
    raise ValueError(
        "This procedure is for one station only."
    )

if weather.duplicated(
    subset=[
        "STATION",
        "DATE"
    ]
).any():
    raise ValueError(
        "Resolve duplicate station-date records first."
    )

if weather[
    "DATE"
].min() < study_start:
    raise ValueError(
        "A date is earlier than the study period."
    )

if weather[
    "DATE"
].max() > study_end:
    raise ValueError(
        "A date is later than the study period."
    )

weather = weather.sort_values(
    "DATE"
)

weather = weather.reset_index(
    drop=True
)
```

### 4.4 Remove Empty Variables

Removed `TAVG` and its attributes only after confirming that they are
entirely missing.

```{python}
empty_columns = [
    "TAVG",
    "TAVG_ATTRIBUTES"
]

for column in empty_columns:

    if weather[
        column
    ].notna().any():

        raise ValueError(
            "This column is not entirely empty: "
            + column
        )

weather = weather.drop(
    columns=empty_columns
)
```

### 4.5 Restore Missing Calendar Dates

`reindex` adds absent dates but does not create rainfall measurements.

```{python}
weather = weather.set_index(
    "DATE"
)

weather = weather.reindex(
    full_date_range
)

weather.index.name = "DATE"

weather = weather.reset_index()

weather[
    "ROW_MISSING"
] = weather[
    "DATE"
].isin(
    missing_dates
)
```

### 4.6 Restore Station Metadata

Fill only station metadata that have one known value in this export.

Do not fill weather measurements or observation attributes.

```{python}
station_columns = [
    "STATION",
    "NAME",
    "LATITUDE",
    "LONGITUDE",
    "ELEVATION"
]

for column in station_columns:

    known_values = (
        weather_raw[
            column
        ]
        .dropna()
        .unique()
    )

    if len(
        known_values
    ) != 1:

        raise ValueError(
            "Review station metadata: "
            + column
        )

    station_value = (
        known_values[0]
    )

    weather[
        column
    ] = weather[
        column
    ].fillna(
        station_value
    )
```

### 4.7 Flag Missing Precipitation

```{python}
weather[
    "PRCP_MISSING"
] = weather[
    "PRCP"
].isna()

weather[
    "PRCP_MISSING"
].value_counts()
```

```{python}
pd.crosstab(
    weather[
        "ROW_MISSING"
    ],
    weather[
        "PRCP_MISSING"
    ]
)
```

### 4.8 Verify the Cleaned Time Series

```{python}
print(
    "First date:",
    weather[
        "DATE"

)

print(
    "Last date:",
    weather[
        "DATE"

)

print(

print(

)

print(
    "Inserted dates:",
    weather[
        "ROW_MISSING"
    ].sum()
)

weather.isna().sum()
```

## Part 5 — Quality-Flag Review

The NOAA attributes contain the measurement flag first and the quality
flag second.

Quality flag `I` means an internal-consistency check failed; it does not
provide a replacement value.[^noaa-flags]

### 5.1 Read the Quality Flags

```{python}
variables = [
    "PRCP",
    "TMAX",
    "TMIN",
    "SNOW",
    "SNWD"
]

quality_flags = pd.DataFrame(
    index=weather.index
)

for variable in variables:

    attribute_column = (
        variable
        + "_ATTRIBUTES"
    )

    attributes = weather[
        attribute_column
    ].astype(
        "string"
    )

    parts = attributes.str.split(
        ","
    )

    quality_flag = (
        parts.str[1]
    )

    quality_flag = (
        quality_flag.str.strip()
    )

    observed_rows = weather[
        variable
    ].notna()

    if quality_flag[
        observed_rows
    ].isna().any():

        raise ValueError(
            "Review the attributes for "
            + variable
        )

    quality_flags[
        variable
    ] = quality_flag
```

### 5.2 List Flagged Observations

```{python}
for variable in variables:

    quality_flag = quality_flags[
        variable
    ]

    flagged_rows = (
        quality_flag.fillna("")
        != ""
    )

    columns_to_show = [
        "DATE",
        variable,
        variable + "_ATTRIBUTES"
    ]

    print(
        "\nVariable:",
        variable
    )

    if flagged_rows.sum() == 0:

        print(
            "No nonblank quality flags."
        )

    else:

        flagged_values = weather.loc[
            flagged_rows,
            columns_to_show
        ]

        print(
            flagged_values.to_string(
                index=False
            )
        )
```

### 5.3 Inspect Trace Precipitation

Measurement flag `T` means trace precipitation, not a missing measurement
or a quality exclusion.[^noaa-flags]

```{python}
attributes = weather[
    "PRCP_ATTRIBUTES"
].astype(
    "string"
)

parts = attributes.str.split(
    ","
)

prcp_measurement_flag = (
    parts.str[0]
)

prcp_measurement_flag = (
    prcp_measurement_flag.str.strip()
)

prcp_measurement_flag = (
    prcp_measurement_flag.astype(
        "string"
    )
)

trace_days = (
    prcp_measurement_flag
    == "T"
)

print(
    "Trace precipitation records:",
    trace_days.sum()
)

weather.loc[
    trace_days.fillna(
        False
    ),
    [
        "DATE",
        "PRCP",
        "PRCP_ATTRIBUTES"
    ]
].head()
```

## Part 6 — Finalize the Cleaned Dataset

### 6.1 Quality-Control Policy

The first-version rule excludes measurements with nonblank quality flags.

Only the affected values become missing; entire dates are not deleted.

This is a conservative analysis choice, not proof that every flagged value
is wrong.[^noaa-flags]

### 6.2 Apply Quality Flags

```{python}
weather_clean = (
    weather.copy()
)

qc_summary = pd.DataFrame(
    index=variables
)

qc_summary.index.name = (
    "Variable"
)

qc_summary[
    "Missing before QC"
] = weather[
    variables
].isna().sum()

qc_summary[
    "Excluded by QC"
] = 0

for variable in variables:

    quality_flag = (
        quality_flags[
            variable
        ]
    )

    has_quality_flag = (
        quality_flag.fillna("")
        != ""
    )

    has_value = (
        weather[
            variable
        ].notna()
    )

    excluded = (
        has_quality_flag
        & has_value
    )

    weather_clean[
        variable
        + "_QC_EXCLUDED"
    ] = excluded

    weather_clean.loc[
        has_quality_flag,
        variable
    ] = float(
        "nan"
    )

    qc_summary.loc[
        variable,
        "Excluded by QC"
    ] = excluded.sum()

qc_summary[
    "Missing after QC"
] = weather_clean[
    variables
].isna().sum()

qc_summary
```

### 6.3 Preserve Trace and Missingness Information

```{python}
weather_clean[
    "PRCP_TRACE"
] = trace_days

weather_clean[
    "PRCP_MISSING"
] = weather_clean[
    "PRCP"
].isna()

weather_clean[
    "PRCP_TRACE"
].value_counts(
    dropna=False
)
```

### 6.4 Basic Physical Checks

Check the negative precipitation and snow amounts, inconsistent daily
minimum/maximum temperatures, and infinite values.

Large rainfall values are not removed merely because they are unusual.

```{python}
negative_prcp = (
    weather_clean[
        "PRCP"
    ]
    < 0
).sum()

negative_snow = (
    weather_clean[
        "SNOW"
    ]
    < 0
).sum()

negative_snwd = (
    weather_clean[
        "SNWD"
    ]
    < 0
).sum()

bad_temperatures = (
    weather_clean[
        "TMIN"
    ]
    > weather_clean[
        "TMAX"
    ]
).sum()

infinite_values = 0

for variable in variables:

    positive_inf = (
        weather_clean[
            variable
        ]
        == float(
            "inf"
        )
    ).sum()

    negative_inf = (
        weather_clean[
            variable
        ]
        == float(
            "-inf"
        )
    ).sum()

    infinite_values = (
        infinite_values
        + positive_inf
        + negative_inf
    )

physical_checks = pd.DataFrame()

physical_checks[
    "Check"
] = [
    "Negative PRCP",
    "Negative SNOW",
    "Negative SNWD",
    "TMIN greater than TMAX",
    "Infinite measurements"
]

physical_checks[
    "Count"
] = [
    negative_prcp,
    negative_snow,
    negative_snwd,
    bad_temperatures,
    infinite_values
]

physical_checks
```

```{python}
if physical_checks[
    "Count"
].sum() != 0:

    raise ValueError(
        "Review the physical checks before saving."
    )

print(
    "Basic physical checks passed."
)
```

### 6.5 Units and Column Definitions

The original measurement names and metric units are retained.[^noaa-flags]

| Column | Meaning | Unit or coding |
|---|---|---|
| `PRCP` | Daily precipitation | mm |
| `TMAX`, `TMIN` | Daily maximum/minimum temperature | degrees Celsius |
| `SNOW`, `SNWD` | Snowfall / snow depth | mm |
| `ROW_MISSING` | Date absent from source CSV | True / False |
| `PRCP_MISSING` | Precipitation unavailable after QC | True / False |
| `PRCP_TRACE` | Recorded trace flag | True / False / missing |
| `*_QC_EXCLUDED` | Existing value excluded by QC rule | True / False |
| `*_ATTRIBUTES` | Original observation attributes | Unchanged text |

### 6.6 Save the Cleaned Dataset

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

processed_dir = Path(
    "Data/Processed"
)

processed_dir.mkdir(
    parents=True,
    exist_ok=True
)

output_path = (
    "Data/Processed/"
    "seattle_sand_point_cleaned_2015_2025.csv"
)

weather_clean.to_csv(
    output_path,
    index=False,
    date_format="%Y-%m-%d",
    na_rep="",
    encoding="utf-8"
)

print(
    "Saved:",
    output_path
)

print(
    "Rows:",
    len(
        weather_clean
    )
)

print(
    "Columns:",
    weather_clean.shape[1]
)
```

## Part 7 — Exploratory Data Analysis

This section examines data coverage, daily precipitation, its distribution,
and seasonal differences.

It describes one station during 2015–2025, not observed flood events.

### 7.1 Prepare the EDA Data

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

eda = weather_clean[
    [
        "DATE",
        "PRCP"
    ]
].copy()

eda = eda.sort_values(
    "DATE"
)

eda[
    "YEAR"
] = eda[
    "DATE"
].dt.year

eda[
    "MONTH"
] = eda[
    "DATE"
].dt.month

if eda[
    "PRCP"
].notna().sum() == 0:

    raise ValueError(
        "No precipitation observations are available for EDA."
    )
```

### 7.2 Check Monthly Coverage Before Calculating Totals

A month is included in monthly-total comparisons only if every day has a
retained precipitation value.

Available days from incomplete months remain in the daily analysis.

```{python}
monthly_groups = (
    eda.groupby(
        [
            "YEAR",
            "MONTH"
        ]
    )
)

monthly = pd.DataFrame()

monthly[
    "expected_days"
] = monthly_groups.size()

monthly[
    "observed_days"
] = monthly_groups[
    "PRCP"
].count()

monthly[
    "observed_sum_mm"
] = monthly_groups[
    "PRCP"
].sum(
    min_count=1
)

monthly = monthly.reset_index()

monthly[
    "missing_days"
] = (
    monthly[
        "expected_days"
    ]
    - monthly[
        "observed_days"
    ]
)

monthly[
    "coverage_pct"
] = (
    100
    * monthly[
        "observed_days"
    ]
    / monthly[
        "expected_days"
    ]
)

monthly[
    "complete"
] = (
    monthly[
        "observed_days"
    ]
    == monthly[
        "expected_days"
    ]
)

monthly[
    "total_mm"
] = monthly[
    "observed_sum_mm"
]

incomplete_months = (
    monthly[
        "complete"
    ]
    == False
)

monthly.loc[
    incomplete_months,
    "total_mm"
] = float(
    "nan"
)

coverage_columns = [
    "YEAR",
    "MONTH",
    "expected_days",
    "observed_days",
    "missing_days",
    "coverage_pct"
]

monthly.loc[
    incomplete_months,
    coverage_columns
].round(
    2
)
```

### 7.6 Interpretation Boundaries

These summaries describe this station sample, not precipitation at every
Seattle location.

Missing measurements have not been estimated.

Large daily rainfall is not itself evidence of flooding.

These plots do not establish flood occurrence, flood mechanisms, or
long-term climate trends.

### 7.7 EDA Findings

Among the 3,987 available daily precipitation records, the mean is about
2.72 mm, the median is 0 mm, and the maximum is 67.1 mm.

The distribution is strongly right-skewed.

The complete-month comparison uses 129 of the 132 year-months.

December has the highest sample mean monthly total, about 163.48 mm, while
July has the lowest, about 9.16 mm.

These are descriptive results for this station and study period.

## Part 8 — Rainfall Feature Engineering

### 8.1 Define the Time Convention

Let $P_t$ be the reported precipitation for date $t$.

We construct:

$$
R_{1,t}
=
P_{t-1}
$$

$$
R_{3,t}
=
P_{t-1}
+
P_{t-2}
+
P_{t-3}
$$

$$
R_{7,t}
=
\sum_{i=1}^{7}
P_{t-i}
$$

These features exclude $P_t$.

The provisional prediction convention is to use observations through date
$t-1$ when predicting an outcome labeled date $t$.

The 1-, 3-, and 7-day windows are starting choices, not proven optimal
hydrologic windows.

### 8.2 Prepare the Feature Table

```{python}
features = weather_clean[
    [
        "STATION",
        "DATE",
        "PRCP"
    ]
].copy()

features = features.sort_values(
    "DATE"
)

features = features.reset_index(
    drop=True
)

expected_dates = pd.Series(
    full_date_range
)

if not features[
    "DATE"
].equals(
    expected_dates
):

    raise ValueError(
        "Keep one row per calendar day before creating features."
    )
```

### 8.3 Previous-Day Precipitation

With the complete daily calendar, shifting values down one row places the
previous day's precipitation beside the current date. The dates themselves
stay unchanged.[^pandas-shift]

```{python}
features[
    "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM"
] = features[
    "PRCP"
].shift(
    1
)

features[
    [
        "DATE",
        "PRCP",
        "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM"
    ]
].head(
    10
)
```

### 8.4 Previous Three-Day Precipitation

Apply the rolling sum to the already shifted precipitation series.

`min_periods=3` requires all three calendar-day values to be available;
otherwise the feature remains missing.[^pandas-rolling]

```{python}
previous_rain = (
    features[
        "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM"
    ]
)

window_3d = (
    previous_rain.rolling(
        window=3,
        min_periods=3
    )
)

features[
    "RAIN_PREV_3D_MM"
] = window_3d.sum()
```

### 8.5 Previous Seven-Day Precipitation

The seven-day feature uses the same shifted rainfall series and requires
all seven previous calendar-day values to be available.[^pandas-rolling]

```{python}
window_7d = (
    previous_rain.rolling(
        window=7,
        min_periods=7
    )
)

features[
    "RAIN_PREV_7D_MM"
] = window_7d.sum()

display_columns = [
    "DATE",
    "PRCP",
    "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM",
    "RAIN_PREV_3D_MM",
    "RAIN_PREV_7D_MM"
]

features[
    display_columns
].head(
    10
)
```

For January 8, 2015, the three-day feature uses January 5–7 and the
seven-day feature uses January 1–7.

Neither includes January 8.

### 8.6 Visualize the Rainfall-History Features

To make the feature construction easier to interpret, we display a short
example period rather than the entire 2015–2025 record.

The 1-day feature represents precipitation on the previous calendar day.

The 3-day and 7-day features accumulate precipitation over progressively
longer histories.

All three exclude precipitation reported for the target date itself.

```{python}
#| label: fig-rainfall-history-features
#| fig-cap: "Example of previous 1-, 3-, and 7-day rainfall-history features at Seattle Sand Point. Each feature uses precipitation before the date shown."
#| fig-align: center

feature_plot_start = pd.Timestamp(
    "2015-01-01"
)

feature_plot_end = pd.Timestamp(
    "2015-02-15"
)

feature_plot_rows = (
    features[
        "DATE"
    ].between(
        feature_plot_start,
        feature_plot_end
    )
)

feature_plot = (
    features.loc[
        feature_plot_rows,
        [
            "DATE",
            "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM",
            "RAIN_PREV_3D_MM",
            "RAIN_PREV_7D_MM"
        ]
    ].copy()
)

plt.figure(
    figsize=(
        10,
        5
    )
)

plt.plot(
    feature_plot[
        "DATE"
    ],
    feature_plot[
        "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM"
    ],
    label="Previous 1 day",
    linewidth=1.2
)

plt.plot(
    feature_plot[
        "DATE"
    ],
    feature_plot[
        "RAIN_PREV_3D_MM"
    ],
    label="Previous 3 days",
    linewidth=1.2
)

plt.plot(
    feature_plot[
        "DATE"
    ],
    feature_plot[
        "RAIN_PREV_7D_MM"
    ],
    label="Previous 7 days",
    linewidth=1.2
)

plt.title(
    "Example Rainfall-History Features"
)

plt.xlabel(
    "Date"
)

plt.ylabel(
    "Accumulated precipitation (mm)"
)

plt.ylim(
    bottom=0
)

plt.legend()

plt.tight_layout()

plt.show()
```

The longer windows are smoother because each value contains rainfall from
multiple preceding calendar days.

A large seven-day value therefore does not mean that all precipitation
occurred on the date shown.

The first rows are missing by design because the study period does not
contain enough earlier observations to construct complete histories.

## Part 9 — Hydrologic Outcome Data

### 9.1 Source and Scope

Use the daily export for King County site `58A`, requested for
January 1, 2015 through December 31, 2025.

The source file is `Hydrology_TOVMP.csv`.

King County describes its daily streamflow product as average daily stream
discharge rates.[^kc-daily-flow]

The CSV reports stage in feet and discharge in cubic feet per second.

The exact daily time boundaries, daylight-saving convention, and historical
publication timing are not specified in this export.

### 9.2 Load the Long Record

```{python}
streamflow_raw = pd.read_csv(
    "Data/Raw/Hydrology_TOVMP.csv"
)

print(
    "Raw dimensions:",
    streamflow_raw.shape
)

streamflow_raw.head()
```

### 9.3 Prepare a Working Copy

```{python}
streamflow = (
    streamflow_raw.copy()
)

streamflow = (
    streamflow.rename(
        columns={
            "Site_Code":
                "SITE_ID",

            "Collect Date (local)":
                "DATE_LOCAL",

            "Stage (ft)":
                "STAGE_FT",

            "Discharge (cfs)":
                "FLOW_CFS",

            "E = Estimate; W = Warning; P = Provisional":
                "FLAG"
        }
    )
)

streamflow[
    "DATE_LOCAL"
] = pd.to_datetime(
    streamflow[
        "DATE_LOCAL"
    ],
    format="%m/%d/%Y"
)

streamflow[
    "STAGE_FT"
] = pd.to_numeric(
    streamflow[
        "STAGE_FT"
    ],
    errors="raise"
)

streamflow[
    "FLOW_CFS"
] = pd.to_numeric(
    streamflow[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ],
    errors="raise"
)

if streamflow[
    "SITE_ID"
].isna().any():

    raise ValueError(
        "A station ID is missing."
    )

if not (
    streamflow[
        "SITE_ID"
    ]
    == "58A"
).all():

    raise ValueError(
        "This section expects only site 58A."
    )

if streamflow[
    "DATE_LOCAL"
].isna().any():

    raise ValueError(
        "A record has no date."
    )

if streamflow.duplicated(
    subset=[
        "SITE_ID",
        "DATE_LOCAL"
    ]
).any():

    raise ValueError(
        "Review duplicate station-date records."
    )

streamflow = (
    streamflow.sort_values(
        "DATE_LOCAL"
    )
)

streamflow = (
    streamflow.reset_index(
        drop=True
    )
)
```

### 9.4 Check Dates and Missing Measurements

```{python}
flow_calendar = pd.date_range(

missing_flow_dates = (

)

if outside_period.any():

    )

print(
    "Recorded rows:",
    len(
        streamflow
    )
)

print(
    "Missing calendar dates:",
    len(
        missing_flow_dates
    )

missing_flow_dates
```

```{python}
streamflow[
    [
        "STAGE_FT",
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ]
].isna().sum()
```

### 9.5 Inspect and Preserve the Flags

The CSV header defines:

- `P` as Provisional;
- `E` as Estimate;
- `W` as Warning.

This export contains `P` and blank flags.

Blank means no flag was supplied, not proof of final approval.

Provisional measurements are retained in the main analysis.

```{python}
flow_flags = (
    streamflow[
        "FLAG"
    ]
    .astype(
        "string"
    )
)

flow_flags = (
    flow_flags.str.strip()
)

flow_flags = (
    flow_flags.fillna("")
)

unreviewed_flags = (
    flow_flags.isin(
        [
            "",
            "P"
        ]
    )
    == False
)

if unreviewed_flags.any():

    raise ValueError(
        "Review additional flag types before continuing."
    )

streamflow[
    "PROVISIONAL_FLAG"
] = (
    flow_flags
    == "P"
)

flag_labels = (
    flow_flags.replace(
        "",
        "Blank in export"
    )
)

flag_labels.value_counts()
```

### 9.6 Restore the Daily Calendar

Missing dates are added without estimating stage or discharge.

```{python}
streamflow = (
    streamflow.set_index(
        "DATE_LOCAL"
    )
)

streamflow = (
    streamflow.reindex(
        flow_calendar
    )
)

streamflow.index.name = (
    "DATE_LOCAL"
)

streamflow = (
    streamflow.reset_index()
)

streamflow[
    "SITE_ID"
] = streamflow[
    "SITE_ID"
].fillna(
    "58A"
)

streamflow[
    "FLOW_ROW_MISSING"
] = streamflow[
    "DATE_LOCAL"
].isin(
    missing_flow_dates
)

streamflow[
    "FLOW_MISSING"
] = streamflow[
    "FLOW_CFS"
].isna()

print(
    "Calendar rows:",
    len(
        streamflow
    )
)

print(
    "Available discharge values:",
    streamflow[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ].count()
)

print(
    "Missing discharge values:",
    streamflow[
        "FLOW_MISSING"
    ].sum()
)

streamflow[
    "PROVISIONAL_FLAG"
].value_counts(
    dropna=False
)
```

### 9.7 Check Coverage by Year

```{python}
flow_years = (
    streamflow[

flow_groups = (
    streamflow.groupby(

flow_coverage[
```

### 9.10 Flow Data Findings

The long export contains 3,974 records.

The requested calendar has 4,018 days, so 44 dates are absent.

The gaps are:

- December 22–25, 2021: 4 days;
- January 14–30, 2022: 17 days;
- July 8–30, 2023: 23 days.

All existing rows contain stage and discharge values.

There are 753 provisional records and 3,221 records with blank flags.

The largest exported daily discharge is 68.15 cfs on December 5, 2023;
that record is provisional.

After calendar standardization, there are 4,018 rows and 44 missing
stage and discharge values.

## Part 10 — Data Alignment and Matched-Sample Audit

### 10.1 Pairing Definition and Limitations

Prepare a candidate pairing between Sand Point rainfall history and
site 58A discharge.

The response for date $t$ is reported daily mean flow.

Candidate rainfall inputs are the 1-, 3-, and 7-day rainfall histories
ending on date $t-1$.

Matching date labels does not establish identical daily observation
intervals or catchment-wide rainfall representativeness.

### 10.2 Review Rainfall Observation-Time Labels

The fourth NOAA precipitation attribute field is the observation time when
supplied.[^noaa-flags]

A value of `2400` is not a data-publication timestamp.

```{python}
rain_attributes = (
    weather_clean[
        "PRCP_ATTRIBUTES"
    ]
    .astype(
        "string"
    )
)

rain_parts = (
    rain_attributes.str.split(
        ","
    )
)

rain_observation_time = (
    rain_parts.str[3]
)

rain_observation_time.value_counts(
    dropna=False
)
```

### 10.3 Prepare the Rainfall Table

```{python}
rainfall_match = (
    features.copy()
)

rainfall_match = (
    rainfall_match.rename(
        columns={
            "STATION":
                "WEATHER_STATION"
        }
    )
)

rainfall_match.head()
```

### 10.4 Prepare the Flow Table

Same-day stage is not included as an advance predictor.

```{python}
flow_columns = [
    "DATE_LOCAL",
    "SITE_ID",
    "FLOW_CFS",
    "FLAG",
    "PROVISIONAL_FLAG",
    "FLOW_ROW_MISSING",
    "FLOW_MISSING"
]

flow_match = (
    streamflow[
        flow_columns
    ].copy()
)

flow_match = (
    flow_match.rename(
        columns={
            "SITE_ID":
                "FLOW_SITE_ID",

            "FLAG":
                "FLOW_FLAG"
        }
    )
)

flow_match.head()
```

### 10.5 Pair Records by Reported Date Labels

The outer join preserves all date labels, while `validate="one_to_one"`
requires each date key to appear at most once in each input table.[^pandas-merge]

```{python}
paired = pd.merge(
    rainfall_match,
    flow_match,
    left_on="DATE",
    right_on="DATE_LOCAL",
    how="outer",
    validate="one_to_one"
)

paired = paired.sort_values(
    "DATE"
)

paired = paired.reset_index(
    drop=True
)

print(
    "Calendar rows in the candidate pairing:",
    len(
        paired
    )
)

paired.head()
```

### 10.6 Count Complete Candidate Pairs

`PAIR_COMPLETE` means all three rainfall features and the flow response are
available.

It is not a quality-approval flag.

```{python}
predictor_columns = [
    "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM",
    "RAIN_PREV_3D_MM",
    "RAIN_PREV_7D_MM"
]

paired[
    "HAS_RAIN_HISTORY"
] = paired[
    predictor_columns
].notna().all(
    axis=1
)

paired[
    "HAS_FLOW"
] = paired[
    "FLOW_CFS"
].notna()

paired[
    "PAIR_COMPLETE"
] = (
    paired[
        "HAS_RAIN_HISTORY"
    ]
    & paired[
        "HAS_FLOW"
    ]
)

print(
    "Complete rainfall histories:",
    paired[
        "HAS_RAIN_HISTORY"
    ].sum()
)

print(
    "Available flow values:",
    paired[
        "HAS_FLOW"
    ].sum()
)

print(
    "Complete candidate pairs:",
    paired[
        "PAIR_COMPLETE"
    ].sum()
)

pd.crosstab(
    paired[
        "HAS_RAIN_HISTORY"
    ],
    paired[
        "HAS_FLOW"
    ]
)
```

### 10.7 Preserve Provisional Status

```{python}
complete_pairs = (
    paired[
        "PAIR_COMPLETE"
    ]
)

paired_status = (
    paired.loc[
        complete_pairs,
        "PROVISIONAL_FLAG"
    ]
)

paired_status.value_counts(
    dropna=False
)
```

```{python}
Path(
    "Data/Processed"
).mkdir(
    parents=True,
    exist_ok=True
)

paired_path = (
    "Data/Processed/"
    "sand_point_58A_candidate_pairs_2015_2025.csv"
)

paired.to_csv(
    paired_path,
    index=False,
    date_format="%Y-%m-%d",
    na_rep="",
    encoding="utf-8"
)

print(
    "Saved:",
    paired_path

```

### 10.9 Alignment Assumptions

The pairing does not establish that Sand Point rainfall represents the
entire upstream catchment or that the rainfall and flow products use
identical daily intervals.

Where exact historical availability cannot be reconstructed, the project
is interpreted as a retrospective experiment under the stated timing
assumption rather than as a verified operational forecast.

# Statistical Models

## Part 11 — Prediction Design and Baseline Models

### 11.1 Define the Experiment

The response is daily mean discharge at site 58A in cfs.

The rainfall models use only:

- `RAIN_PREV_1D_MM`;
- `RAIN_PREV_3D_MM`;
- `RAIN_PREV_7D_MM`.

Same-day precipitation and same-day stage are not predictors.

The experiment assumes observations labeled with date $t-1$ are available
before predicting flow labeled date $t$.

### 11.2 Fix the Training, Validation, and Test Periods

| Dataset | Dates | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Training | 2015-01-01 to 2021-12-31 | Estimate model parameters |
| Validation | 2022-01-01 to 2023-12-31 | Compare candidate methods |
| Test | 2024-01-01 to 2025-12-31 | Final evaluation |

Dates are not randomly shuffled.

All fitted preprocessing quantities must be estimated from the training
period during model development.[^time-design]

Earlier descriptive analysis included the full period.

Therefore the test period is not completely unseen in every descriptive
sense, but its prediction errors are excluded from model selection.

### 11.3 Prepare the Daily Experiment Table

Previous-day flow is created before removing incomplete rows.

```{python}
model_calendar = (
    paired.copy()
)

model_calendar = (
    model_calendar.sort_values(
        "DATE"
    )
)

model_calendar = (
    model_calendar.reset_index(
        drop=True
    )
)

expected_dates = pd.Series(
    full_date_range
)

if not model_calendar[
    "DATE"
].equals(
    expected_dates
):

    raise ValueError(
        "Restore the full daily calendar before computing flow lags."
    )

model_calendar[
    "FLOW_PREV_1D_CFS"
] = model_calendar[
    "FLOW_CFS"
].shift(
    1
)

model_calendar[
    "FLOW_PREV_1D_PROVISIONAL"
] = model_calendar[
    "PROVISIONAL_FLAG"
].shift(
    1
)

model_calendar[
    "MONTH"
] = model_calendar[
    "DATE"
].dt.month
```

### 11.4 Define a Common Comparison Sample

Every method is initially evaluated on dates where:

- all three rainfall histories are available;
- current flow is available;
- previous-day flow is available.

```{python}
rain_predictors = [
    "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM",
    "RAIN_PREV_3D_MM",
    "RAIN_PREV_7D_MM"
]

required_values = (
    rain_predictors
    + [
        "FLOW_CFS",
        "FLOW_PREV_1D_CFS"
    ]
)

model_calendar[
    "COMPARISON_COMPLETE"
] = model_calendar[
    required_values
].notna().all(
    axis=1
)

print(
    "Complete rainfall-flow pairs:",
    model_calendar[
        "PAIR_COMPLETE"
    ].sum()
)

print(
    "Common comparison rows:",
    model_calendar[
        "COMPARISON_COMPLETE"
    ].sum()
)
```

### 11.5 Assign Periods and Audit Coverage

```{python}
model_calendar[
    "SPLIT"
] = "Unassigned"

train_dates = (
    model_calendar[
        "DATE"
    ].between(
        "2015-01-01",
        "2021-12-31"
    )
)

validation_dates = (
    model_calendar[
        "DATE"
    ].between(
        "2022-01-01",
        "2023-12-31"
    )
)

test_dates = (
    model_calendar[
        "DATE"
    ].between(
        "2024-01-01",
        "2025-12-31"
    )
)

model_calendar.loc[
    train_dates,
    "SPLIT"
] = "Train"

model_calendar.loc[
    validation_dates,
    "SPLIT"
] = "Validation"

model_calendar.loc[
    test_dates,
    "SPLIT"
] = "Test"

if (
    model_calendar[
        "SPLIT"
    ]
    == "Unassigned"
).any():

    raise ValueError(
        "Assign every date to an evaluation period."
    )

split_names = [
    "Train",
    "Validation",
    "Test"
]

summary_columns = [
    "Calendar days",
    "Rain-flow pairs",
    "Common sample",
    "Provisional targets"
]

split_summary = pd.DataFrame(
    index=split_names,
    columns=summary_columns
)

for split_name in split_names:

    period_rows = (
        model_calendar[
            "SPLIT"
        ]
        == split_name
    )

    period = (
        model_calendar.loc[
            period_rows
        ]
    )

    eligible = (
        period.loc[
            period[
                "COMPARISON_COMPLETE"
            ]
        ]
    )

    split_summary.loc[
        split_name,
        "Calendar days"
    ] = len(
        period
    )

    split_summary.loc[
        split_name,
        "Rain-flow pairs"
    ] = period[
        "PAIR_COMPLETE"
    ].sum()

    split_summary.loc[
        split_name,
        "Common sample"
    ] = len(
        eligible
    )

    split_summary.loc[
        split_name,
        "Provisional targets"
    ] = eligible[
        "PROVISIONAL_FLAG"
    ].sum()

split_summary = (
    split_summary.astype(
        int
    )
)

split_summary
```

### 11.6 Create the Three Data Subsets

```{python}
comparison_data = (
    model_calendar.loc[
        model_calendar[
            "COMPARISON_COMPLETE"
        ]
    ].copy()
)

train = (
    comparison_data.loc[
        comparison_data[
            "SPLIT"
        ]
        == "Train"
    ].copy()
)

validation = (
    comparison_data.loc[
        comparison_data[
            "SPLIT"
        ]
        == "Validation"
    ].copy()
)

test = (
    comparison_data.loc[
        comparison_data[
            "SPLIT"
        ]
        == "Test"
    ].copy()
)

if (
    train.empty
    or validation.empty
    or test.empty
):

    raise ValueError(
        "An evaluation subset has no usable observations."
    )

print(
    "Training rows:",
    len(
        train
    )
)

print(
    "Validation rows:",
    len(
        validation
    )
)

print(
    "Reserved test rows:",
    len(
        test
    )
)
```

### 11.7 Baseline 1: Training Mean

The first benchmark predicts the training-sample mean for every validation
date.[^simple-baselines]

$$
\widehat Q_t^{\mathrm{mean}}
=
\overline Q_{\mathrm{train}}
$$

```{python}
training_mean = (
    train[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ].mean()
)

validation_predictions = (
    validation.copy()
)

validation_predictions[
    "PRED_MEAN_CFS"
] = training_mean

print(
    "Training mean discharge (cfs):",
    round(
        training_mean,
        3
    )
)
```

### 11.8 Baseline 2: Training Calendar-Month Mean

The second benchmark uses the training-sample mean daily flow for the
calendar month being predicted.[^simple-baselines]

```{python}
training_month_means = (
    train.groupby(
        "MONTH"
    )[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ].mean()
)

if len(
    training_month_means
) != 12:

    raise ValueError(
        "The monthly baseline needs training observations in every month."
    )

validation_predictions[
    "PRED_MONTH_MEAN_CFS"
] = float(
    "nan"
)

for month in range(
    1,
    13
):

    month_rows = (
        validation_predictions[
            "MONTH"
        ]
        == month
    )

    month_mean = (
        training_month_means.loc[
            month
        ]
    )

    validation_predictions.loc[
        month_rows,
        "PRED_MONTH_MEAN_CFS"
    ] = month_mean
```

### 11.9 Baseline 3: Previous-Day Flow

The persistence benchmark predicts the previous day's reported
flow.[^simple-baselines]

$$
\widehat Q_t^{\mathrm{persistence}}
=
Q_{t-1}
$$

```{python}
validation_predictions[
    "PRED_PERSISTENCE_CFS"
] = validation_predictions[
    "FLOW_PREV_1D_CFS"
]
```

Persistence uses recent streamflow rather than rainfall.

Therefore its comparison with rainfall-only models does not isolate the
incremental value of rainfall after streamflow history is already known.

### 11.10 Evaluate the Validation Period

MAE is the primary overall error measure.

RMSE is also reported because it gives larger errors more influence.[^baseline-errors]

$$
\mathrm{MAE}
=
\frac{1}{n}
\sum_{i=1}^{n}
\left|
Q_i-\widehat Q_i
\right|
$$

$$
\mathrm{RMSE}
=
\sqrt{
\frac{1}{n}
\sum_{i=1}^{n}
\left(
Q_i-\widehat Q_i
\right)^2
}
$$

```{python}
baseline_columns = {
    "Training mean":
        "PRED_MEAN_CFS",

    "Calendar-month mean":
        "PRED_MONTH_MEAN_CFS",

    "Previous-day flow":
        "PRED_PERSISTENCE_CFS"
}

baseline_results = pd.DataFrame(
    index=list(
        baseline_columns
    )
)

baseline_results[
    "Validation days"
] = len(
    validation_predictions
)

for baseline_name in baseline_columns:

    prediction_column = (
        baseline_columns[
            baseline_name
        ]
    )

    predicted = (
        validation_predictions[
            prediction_column
        ]
    )

    if predicted.isna().any():

        raise ValueError(
            "A baseline prediction is missing."
        )

    errors = (
        validation_predictions[
            "FLOW_CFS"
        ]
        - predicted
    )

    absolute_errors = (
        errors.abs()
    )

    squared_errors = (
        errors ** 2
    )

    baseline_results.loc[
        baseline_name,
        "MAE_cfs"
    ] = absolute_errors.mean()

    baseline_results.loc[
        baseline_name,
        "RMSE_cfs"
    ] = (
        squared_errors.mean()
        ** 0.5
    )

baseline_results.round(
    3
)
```

```{python}
)
```

### 11.12 Baseline Findings

On the 2022–2023 validation sample:

- the training mean has MAE about 4.603 cfs;
- the calendar-month mean has MAE about 3.673 cfs;
- previous-day flow has MAE about 2.557 cfs.

Persistence is therefore a strong benchmark for this prediction task.

## Part 12 — Linear Regression and Diagnostics

### 12.1 Model Specification

Model 1 uses previous-day rainfall:

$$
Q_t
=
a_0
+
a_1R_{1,t}
+
\varepsilon_t.
$$

Model 2 uses three rainfall-history totals:

$$
Q_t
=
b_0
+
b_1R_{1,t}
+
b_3R_{3,t}
+
b_7R_{7,t}
+
\varepsilon_t.
$$

These are statistical prediction models rather than physical runoff
equations.

### 12.2 Ordinary Least Squares

OLS chooses coefficients that minimize the sum of squared training
residuals.[^ols-estimation]

The statsmodels OLS interface does not automatically add an intercept, so
we add the constant column explicitly.[^statsmodels-ols]

```{python}
import statsmodels.api as sm

X_train = (
    train[
        rain_predictors
    ].copy()
)

y_train = (
    train[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ].copy()
)

X_validation = (
    validation[
        rain_predictors
    ].copy()
)

y_validation = (
    validation[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ].copy()
)

print(
    "Training rows:",
    len(
        X_train
    )
)

print(
    "Validation rows:",
    len(
        X_validation
    )
)
```

### 12.3 Inspect Predictor Correlations

The rainfall windows overlap.

```{python}
predictor_correlations = (
    X_train.corr()
)

predictor_correlations.round(
    3
)
```

### 12.4 Fit Model 1

```{python}
X_train_simple = (
    X_train[
        [
            "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM"
        ]
    ].copy()
)

X_validation_simple = (
    X_validation[
        [
            "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM"
        ]
    ].copy()
)

X_train_simple = sm.add_constant(
    X_train_simple,
    has_constant="add"
)

X_validation_simple = sm.add_constant(
    X_validation_simple,
    has_constant="add"
)

simple_model = sm.OLS(
    y_train,
    X_train_simple,
    missing="raise"
)

simple_fit = (
    simple_model.fit()
)

simple_coefficients = (
    simple_fit.params.to_frame(
        name="Estimate"
    )
)

simple_coefficients
```

### 12.5 Fit Model 2

```{python}
X_train_multiple = sm.add_constant(
    X_train,
    has_constant="add"
)

X_validation_multiple = sm.add_constant(
    X_validation,
    has_constant="add"
)

multiple_model = sm.OLS(
    y_train,
    X_train_multiple,
    missing="raise"
)

multiple_fit = (
    multiple_model.fit()
)

multiple_coefficients = (
    multiple_fit.params.to_frame(
        name="Estimate"
    )
)

multiple_coefficients
```

### 12.6 Interpret the Overlapping Rainfall Windows

A multiple-regression coefficient describes a change while other included
predictors are held fixed.[^linear-model]

Because the cumulative windows overlap, adding one mm of rainfall yesterday
changes all three totals.

```{python}
b1 = multiple_fit.params[
    "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM"
]

b3 = multiple_fit.params[
    "RAIN_PREV_3D_MM"
]

b7 = multiple_fit.params[
    "RAIN_PREV_7D_MM"
]

lag_weights = pd.DataFrame(
    index=[
        "1 day earlier",
        "One day at lag 2 or 3",
        "One day at lag 4, 5, 6, or 7"
    ]
)

lag_weights[
    "Predicted change: cfs per mm"
] = [
    b1 + b3 + b7,
    b3 + b7,
    b7
]

lag_weights.round(
    4
)
```

These values are fitted statistical associations, not causal runoff
coefficients.

### 12.7 Inspect Training Fit

```{python}
training_fit = pd.DataFrame(
    index=[
        "One-day rainfall OLS",
        "Three-window rainfall OLS"
    ]
)

training_fit[
    "Training days"
] = len(
    train
)

training_fit[
    "Training R2"
] = [
    simple_fit.rsquared,
    multiple_fit.rsquared
]

training_fit.round(
    3
)
```

### 12.8 Predict the Validation Period

```{python}
if not validation_predictions[
    "DATE"
].equals(
    validation[
        "DATE"
    ]
):

    raise ValueError(
        "Compare models on the same validation dates."
    )

regression_validation = (
    validation_predictions.copy()
)

regression_validation[
    "PRED_SIMPLE_OLS_CFS"
] = simple_fit.predict(
    X_validation_simple
)

regression_validation[
    "PRED_MULTIPLE_OLS_CFS"
] = multiple_fit.predict(
    X_validation_multiple
)

ols_prediction_columns = [
    "PRED_SIMPLE_OLS_CFS",
    "PRED_MULTIPLE_OLS_CFS"
]

if regression_validation[
    ols_prediction_columns
].isna().any().any():

    raise ValueError(
        "A regression prediction is missing."
    )

negative_predictions = (
    regression_validation[
        ols_prediction_columns
    ]
    < 0
).sum()

negative_predictions
```

### 12.9 Compare Validation Errors

```{python}
regression_columns = {
    "One-day rainfall OLS":
        "PRED_SIMPLE_OLS_CFS",

    "Three-window rainfall OLS":
        "PRED_MULTIPLE_OLS_CFS"
}

validation_comparison = (
    baseline_results.copy()
)

for model_name in regression_columns:

        y_validation

        model_name,
        "Validation days"
    ] = len(

    validation_comparison.loc[
        model_name,
        "MAE_cfs"
    ] = errors.abs().mean()

    validation_comparison.loc[
        model_name,
        "RMSE_cfs"
    ] = (
        (
            errors ** 2
        ).mean()
        ** 0.5
    )

validation_comparison[
    "Validation days"
] = (
    validation_comparison[
        "Validation days"
    ].astype(
        int
    )
)

validation_comparison.round(
    3
)
```

### 12.11 Training Residuals versus Fitted Values

Residuals are observed minus fitted flow.

```{python}
training_diagnostics = (
    train[
        [
            "DATE",
            "FLOW_CFS"
        ]
    ].copy()
)

training_diagnostics[
    "FITTED_CFS"
] = multiple_fit.fittedvalues

training_diagnostics[
    "RESIDUAL_CFS"
] = (
    training_diagnostics[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ]
    - training_diagnostics[
        "FITTED_CFS"
    ]
)

print(
    "Mean training residual (cfs):",
    round(
        training_diagnostics[
            "RESIDUAL_CFS"
        ].mean(),
        6
    )
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-ols-training-residuals
#| fig-cap: "Training residuals from the three-window rainfall OLS model."
#| fig-align: center

plt.figure(

        8,

    )
)

plt.scatter(
    training_diagnostics[
        "FITTED_CFS"
    ],
    training_diagnostics[
        "RESIDUAL_CFS"
    ],
    s=14,
    alpha=0.35
)

plt.axhline(
    0,
    linestyle="--"
)

plt.title(
    "Training Residuals versus Fitted Flow"
)

)

plt.ylabel(

plt.show()
```

### 12.12 Calendar-Day Residual Correlations

```{python}
training_calendar = pd.date_range(
    "2015-01-01",
    "2021-12-31",
    freq="D"
)

residual_calendar = (
    training_diagnostics.set_index(
        "DATE"
    )
)

residual_calendar = (
    residual_calendar.reindex(
        training_calendar
    )
)

current_residual = (
    residual_calendar[
        "RESIDUAL_CFS"
    ]
)

residual_lags = pd.DataFrame(
    index=[
        1,
        3,
        7
    ]
)

residual_lags.index.name = (
    "Calendar lag (days)"
)

for lag in [
    1,
    3,
    7
]:

    earlier_residual = (
        current_residual.shift(
            lag
        )
    )

    available_pairs = (
        current_residual.notna()
        & earlier_residual.notna()
    )

    current_values = (
        current_residual.loc[
            available_pairs
        ]
    )

    earlier_values = (
        earlier_residual.loc[
            available_pairs
        ]
    )

    residual_lags.loc[
        lag,
        "Available pairs"
    ] = available_pairs.sum()

    residual_lags.loc[
        lag,
        "Correlation"
    ] = current_values.corr(
        earlier_values
    )

residual_lags[
    "Available pairs"
] = residual_lags[
    "Available pairs"
].astype(
    int
)

residual_lags.round(
    3
)
```

These correlations are descriptive diagnostics, not significance tests or
proof of independent errors.[^regression-diagnostics]

### 12.14 Findings and Interpretation

Training R-squared rises from about 0.335 for the one-day model to about
0.481 for the three-window model.

The three-window model also improves validation MAE and RMSE relative to
the one-day rainfall model and both mean baselines.

Three-window OLS validation MAE is approximately 2.865 cfs.

Persistence has lower MAE at approximately 2.557 cfs, while three-window
OLS has lower RMSE than persistence.

The one-day training residual correlation is approximately 0.452, indicating
noticeable remaining temporal dependence.

## Part 13 — Regularization and Tree-Based Model Comparison

### 13.1 Purpose and Comparison Rules

We add three rainfall-only candidates:

- ridge regression;
- regression tree;
- random forest.

All use the same three rainfall-history predictors, training dates, and
validation dates as the multiple OLS model.

| Candidate | Fixed settings |
|---|---|
| Ridge | Standardized rainfall features; alpha = 10 |
| Regression tree | Maximum depth = 4; minimum leaf size = 20 |
| Random forest | 300 trees; maximum depth = 6; minimum leaf size = 10; two candidate features per split |

These configurations are fixed comparison choices, not an exhaustive
hyperparameter search.

### 13.2 Prepare Model Inputs

```{python}
import sklearn

from sklearn.linear_model import Ridge

from sklearn.tree import (
    DecisionTreeRegressor,
    export_text
)

from sklearn.ensemble import (
    RandomForestRegressor
)

X_train_ml = (
    train[
        rain_predictors
    ].copy()
)

X_validation_ml = (
    validation[
        rain_predictors
    ].copy()
)

y_train_ml = (
    train[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ].copy()
)

y_validation_ml = (
    validation[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ].copy()
)

if not regression_validation[
    "DATE"
].equals(
    validation[
        "DATE"
    ]
):

    raise ValueError(
        "Keep the same validation dates for every model."
    )

print(
    "scikit-learn version:",
    sklearn.__version__
)

print(
    "Training rows:",
    len(
        X_train_ml
    )
)

print(
    "Validation rows:",
    len(
        X_validation_ml
    )
)
```

### 13.3 Standardize Rainfall Features for Ridge

Training means and standard deviations are reused for validation.[^ml-scaling]

```{python}
rain_training_means = (
    X_train_ml.mean()
)

rain_training_scales = (
    X_train_ml.std(
        ddof=0
    )
)

if (
    rain_training_scales
    == 0
).any():

    raise ValueError(
        "Review a rainfall predictor with no training variation."
    )

X_train_scaled = (
    X_train_ml
    - rain_training_means
) / rain_training_scales

X_validation_scaled = (
    X_validation_ml
    - rain_training_means
) / rain_training_scales

scaling_table = pd.DataFrame(
    index=rain_predictors
)

scaling_table[
    "Training mean (mm)"
] = rain_training_means

scaling_table[
    "Training standard deviation (mm)"
] = rain_training_scales

scaling_table.round(
    3
)
```

### 13.4 Fit Ridge Regression

Ridge regression adds a squared-coefficient penalty to the least-squares
objective.[^ml-ridge]

```{python}
ridge_model = Ridge(
    alpha=10.0,
    fit_intercept=True,
    solver="svd"
)

ridge_model.fit(
    X_train_scaled,
    y_train_ml
)

ml_validation = (
    regression_validation.copy()
)

ml_validation[
    "PRED_RIDGE_CFS"
] = ridge_model.predict(
    X_validation_scaled
)
```

### 13.5 Compare Ridge and OLS Coefficients in Original Units

```{python}
ridge_original_slopes = pd.Series(
    ridge_model.coef_,
    index=rain_predictors
)

ridge_original_slopes = (
    ridge_original_slopes
    / rain_training_scales
)

ridge_original_intercept = (
    ridge_model.intercept_
    - (
        ridge_original_slopes
        * rain_training_means
    ).sum()
)

slope_comparison = pd.DataFrame(
    index=rain_predictors
)

slope_comparison[
    "OLS: cfs per mm"
] = multiple_fit.params.loc[
    rain_predictors
]

slope_comparison[
    "Ridge: cfs per mm"
] = ridge_original_slopes

print(
    "Ridge intercept in original units (cfs):",
    round(
        ridge_original_intercept,
        4
    )
)

slope_comparison.round(
    4
)
```

### 13.6 Fit a Regression Tree

The regression tree recursively partitions the rainfall-feature space and
predicts using training responses within terminal leaves.[^ml-tree]

```{python}
tree_model = DecisionTreeRegressor(
    criterion="squared_error",
    max_depth=4,
    min_samples_leaf=20,
    random_state=42
)

tree_model.fit(
    X_train_ml,
    y_train_ml
)

ml_validation[
    "PRED_TREE_CFS"
] = tree_model.predict(
    X_validation_ml
)

print(
    "Fitted tree depth:",
    tree_model.get_depth()
)

print(
    "Number of leaves:",
    tree_model.get_n_leaves()
)
```

### 13.7 Inspect the Upper Tree Rules

The printed thresholds are statistical splits, not flood thresholds.

`export_text` is used only to display a readable subset of the fitted tree
rules; it does not modify the fitted estimator.[^ml-tree-text]

```{python}
tree_rules = export_text(
    tree_model,
    feature_names=rain_predictors,
    max_depth=2,
    decimals=2
)

print(
    tree_rules
)
```

### 13.8 Fit a Random Forest

The random forest averages predictions across regression trees fitted to
bootstrap samples of the training data.[^ml-forest]

```{python}
forest_model = RandomForestRegressor(
    n_estimators=300,
    criterion="squared_error",
    max_depth=6,
    min_samples_leaf=10,
    max_features=2,
    bootstrap=True,
    oob_score=False,
    random_state=42,
    n_jobs=1
)

forest_model.fit(
    X_train_ml,
    y_train_ml
)

ml_validation[
    "PRED_FOREST_CFS"
] = forest_model.predict(
    X_validation_ml
)
```

### 13.9 Compare All Validation Scores

```{python}
ml_columns = {
    "Ridge rainfall":
        "PRED_RIDGE_CFS",

    "Regression tree rainfall":
        "PRED_TREE_CFS",

    "Random forest rainfall":
        "PRED_FOREST_CFS"
}

all_validation_results = (
    validation_comparison.copy()
)

for model_name in ml_columns:

    prediction_column = (
        ml_columns[
            model_name
        ]
    )

    predicted = (
        ml_validation[
            prediction_column
        ]
    )

    if predicted.isna().any():

        raise ValueError(
            "A candidate prediction is missing."
        )

    errors = (
        y_validation_ml
        - predicted
    )

    all_validation_results.loc[
        model_name,
        "Validation days"
    ] = len(
        y_validation_ml
    )

    all_validation_results.loc[
        model_name,
        "MAE_cfs"
    ] = errors.abs().mean()

    all_validation_results.loc[
        model_name,
        "RMSE_cfs"
    ] = (
        (
            errors ** 2
        ).mean()
        ** 0.5
    )

all_validation_results[
    "Validation days"
] = (
    all_validation_results[
        "Validation days"
    ].astype(
        int
    )
)

all_validation_results.round(
    3
)
```

### 13.10 Compare Training and Validation Error

```{python}
training_predictions = pd.DataFrame(
    index=train.index
)

training_predictions[
    "Three-window rainfall OLS"
] = multiple_fit.fittedvalues

training_predictions[
    "Ridge rainfall"
] = ridge_model.predict(
    X_train_scaled
)

training_predictions[
    "Regression tree rainfall"
] = tree_model.predict(
    X_train_ml
)

training_predictions[
    "Random forest rainfall"
] = forest_model.predict(
    X_train_ml
)

fit_comparison = pd.DataFrame(
    index=training_predictions.columns
)

for model_name in training_predictions.columns:

    training_errors = (
        y_train_ml
        - training_predictions[
            model_name
        ]
    )

    fit_comparison.loc[
        model_name,
        "Training MAE"
    ] = training_errors.abs().mean()

    fit_comparison.loc[
        model_name,
        "Training RMSE"
    ] = (
        (
            training_errors ** 2
        ).mean()
        ** 0.5
    )

    fit_comparison.loc[
        model_name,
        "Validation MAE"
    ] = all_validation_results.loc[
        model_name,
        "MAE_cfs"
    ]

    fit_comparison.loc[
        model_name,
        "Validation RMSE"
    ] = all_validation_results.loc[
        model_name,
        "RMSE_cfs"
    ]

fit_comparison.round(
    3
)
```

### 13.12 Validation Interpretation

The fixed random-forest configuration has the lowest validation MAE and
RMSE among the rainfall-only models.

Persistence nevertheless has the lowest overall validation MAE.

The random forest has the lowest validation RMSE.

Therefore no single method dominates under both validation metrics.

Overall MAE and RMSE do not establish flood-event prediction performance.

# Robustness and Final Evaluation

## Part 14 — Robustness and Higher-Flow Performance

### 14.1 Purpose

The validation comparison summarizes average prediction error across all
retained validation dates.

It does not show whether the conclusions depend strongly on provisional
flow records or whether model errors are different during unusually
high-flow conditions.

Therefore, perform two additional checks:

1. evaluate the fitted models on validation dates whose target and
   previous-day flow values are both unflagged;
2. evaluate performance when observed flow exceeds a threshold defined
   from the training period only.

No model is refitted or tuned in this section.

### 14.2 Define the Common Prediction Columns

```{python}
robustness_prediction_columns = {
    "Training mean":
        "PRED_MEAN_CFS",

    "Calendar-month mean":
        "PRED_MONTH_MEAN_CFS",

    "Previous-day flow":
        "PRED_PERSISTENCE_CFS",

    "One-day rainfall OLS":
        "PRED_SIMPLE_OLS_CFS",

    "Three-window rainfall OLS":
        "PRED_MULTIPLE_OLS_CFS",

    "Ridge rainfall":
        "PRED_RIDGE_CFS",

    "Regression tree rainfall":
        "PRED_TREE_CFS",

    "Random forest rainfall":
        "PRED_FOREST_CFS"
}

for robustness_column in (
    robustness_prediction_columns.values()
):

    if robustness_column not in (
        ml_validation.columns
    ):

        raise ValueError(
            "Missing validation prediction column: "
            + robustness_column
        )
```

### 14.3 Quality-Status Sensitivity Sample

The main experiment retains provisional site-58A observations.

For this sensitivity check, a validation date is retained only when:

- the target flow is not marked provisional;
- previous-day flow is not marked provisional.

This does not mean provisional observations are wrong.

It only asks whether the main validation pattern changes on a more
restricted subset.

```{python}
validation_target_unflagged = (
    ml_validation[
        "PROVISIONAL_FLAG"
    ]
    .eq(
        False
    )
    .fillna(
        False
    )
)

validation_previous_unflagged = (
    ml_validation[
        "FLOW_PREV_1D_PROVISIONAL"
    ]
    .eq(
        False
    )
    .fillna(
        False
    )
)

validation_quality_mask = (
    validation_target_unflagged
    & validation_previous_unflagged
)

validation_quality_subset = (
    ml_validation.loc[
        validation_quality_mask
    ].copy()
)

print(
    "Full validation rows:",
    len(
        ml_validation
    )
)

print(
    "Quality-sensitivity rows:",
    len(
        validation_quality_subset
    )
)
```

### 14.4 Score the Quality-Sensitivity Sample

```{python}
quality_sensitivity_results = pd.DataFrame(
    index=list(
        robustness_prediction_columns
    )
)

quality_sensitivity_results.index.name = (
    "Method"
)

quality_sensitivity_results[
    "Validation days"
] = len(
    validation_quality_subset
)

for method_name in (
    robustness_prediction_columns
):

    prediction_column = (
        robustness_prediction_columns[
            method_name
        ]
    )

    observed = (
        validation_quality_subset[
            "FLOW_CFS"
        ]
    )

    predicted = (
        validation_quality_subset[
            prediction_column
        ]
    )

    errors = (
        observed
        - predicted
    )

    quality_sensitivity_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "MAE_cfs"
    ] = errors.abs().mean()

    quality_sensitivity_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "RMSE_cfs"
    ] = (
        (
            errors ** 2
        ).mean()
        ** 0.5
    )

quality_sensitivity_results.round(
    3
)
```

The models are not refitted on this restricted sample.

Therefore this analysis checks evaluation sensitivity, not the influence
of provisional training observations on fitted coefficients.

### 14.5 Define a Training-Based Higher-Flow Threshold

Higher flow is defined as the 90th percentile of training responses.

$$
q_{0.90}
=
\operatorname{Quantile}_{0.90}
\left(
Q_t:
t\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{train}}
\right).
$$

The threshold is estimated only from the 2015–2021 training period.[^pandas-quantile]

It is a statistical threshold, not an official flood threshold.

```{python}
high_flow_threshold_cfs = (
    train[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ].quantile(
        0.90
    )
)

print(
    "Training 90th-percentile flow threshold (cfs):",
    round(
        high_flow_threshold_cfs,
        3
    )
)
```

### 14.6 Create the Higher-Flow Validation Subset

```{python}
validation_high_flow_mask = (
    ml_validation[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ]
    >= high_flow_threshold_cfs
)

validation_high_flow = (
    ml_validation.loc[
        validation_high_flow_mask
    ].copy()
)

print(
    "Higher-flow validation dates:",
    len(
        validation_high_flow
    )
)

print(
    "Minimum observed flow in subset:",
    round(
        validation_high_flow[
            "FLOW_CFS"
        ].min(),
        3
    )
)

print(
    "Maximum observed flow in subset:",
    round(
        validation_high_flow[
            "FLOW_CFS"
        ].max(),
        3
    )
)
```

### 14.7 Evaluate Higher-Flow Validation Performance

```{python}
high_flow_validation_results = pd.DataFrame(
    index=list(
        robustness_prediction_columns
    )
)

high_flow_validation_results.index.name = (
    "Method"
)

high_flow_validation_results[
    "Higher-flow days"
] = len(
    validation_high_flow
)

for method_name in (
    robustness_prediction_columns
):

    prediction_column = (
        robustness_prediction_columns[
            method_name
        ]
    )

    observed = (
        validation_high_flow[
            "FLOW_CFS"
        ]
    )

    predicted = (
        validation_high_flow[
            prediction_column
        ]
    )

    errors = (
        observed
        - predicted
    )

    high_flow_validation_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "MAE_cfs"
    ] = errors.abs().mean()

    high_flow_validation_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "RMSE_cfs"
    ] = (
        (
            errors ** 2
        ).mean()
        ** 0.5
    )

high_flow_validation_results.round(
    3
)
```

### 14.8 Compare Overall and Higher-Flow MAE

```{python}
validation_robustness_comparison = pd.DataFrame(
    index=list(
        robustness_prediction_columns
    )
)

validation_robustness_comparison.index.name = (
    "Method"
)

validation_robustness_comparison[
    "Overall_MAE_cfs"
] = all_validation_results[
    "MAE_cfs"
]

validation_robustness_comparison[
    "Quality_subset_MAE_cfs"
] = quality_sensitivity_results[
    "MAE_cfs"
]

validation_robustness_comparison[
    "Higher_flow_MAE_cfs"
] = high_flow_validation_results[
    "MAE_cfs"
]

validation_robustness_comparison.round(
    3
)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-validation-high-flow-mae
#| fig-cap: "Validation MAE on all retained dates and on dates above the training-period 90th-percentile flow threshold."
#| fig-align: center

high_flow_plot = (
    validation_robustness_comparison[
        [
            "Overall_MAE_cfs",
            "Higher_flow_MAE_cfs"
        ]
    ].copy()
)

high_flow_plot = (
    high_flow_plot.sort_values(
        "Overall_MAE_cfs",
        ascending=True
    )
)

plot_positions = list(
    range(
        len(
            high_flow_plot
        )
    )
)

bar_width = 0.38

plt.figure(
    figsize=(
        10,
        6
    )
)

plt.barh(
    [
        position
        - bar_width / 2
        for position in (
            plot_positions
        )
    ],
    high_flow_plot[
        "Overall_MAE_cfs"
    ],
    height=bar_width,
    label="All validation dates"
)

plt.barh(
    [
        position
        + bar_width / 2
        for position in (
            plot_positions
        )
    ],
    high_flow_plot[
        "Higher_flow_MAE_cfs"
    ],
    height=bar_width,
    label="Higher-flow dates"
)

plt.yticks(
    plot_positions,
    high_flow_plot.index
)

plt.xlabel(
    "MAE (cfs)"
)

plt.ylabel(
    "Method"
)

plt.title(
    "Overall and Higher-Flow Validation Error"
)

plt.legend()

plt.tight_layout()

plt.show()
```

### 14.9 Robustness Findings

The quality-status sensitivity sample contains 236 validation dates.

Approximate MAE on this restricted sample is:

| Method | MAE (cfs) |
|---|---:|
| Previous-day flow | 1.984 |
| Random forest rainfall | 2.097 |
| Regression tree rainfall | 2.156 |
| Three-window rainfall OLS | 2.309 |
| Ridge rainfall | 2.312 |

The main validation pattern therefore remains broadly similar after the
quality-status restriction.

The training-period 90th-percentile flow threshold is approximately:

$$
19.368\ \text{cfs}.
$$

Forty validation dates meet or exceed this threshold.

Approximate higher-flow MAE is:

| Method | Higher-flow MAE (cfs) |
|---|---:|
| Random forest rainfall | 9.892 |
| Regression tree rainfall | 9.946 |
| Three-window rainfall OLS | 10.439 |
| Ridge rainfall | 10.448 |
| One-day rainfall OLS | 11.456 |
| Previous-day flow | 13.820 |

Persistence has the lowest overall validation MAE but does not have the
lowest MAE on the higher-flow subset.

This does not establish flood-warning performance because the subset uses
daily mean discharge and contains only 40 dates.

## Part 15 — Final Test Evaluation

### 15.1 Freeze the Evaluation Policy

The reserved test period covers January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2025.

The following choices remain fixed before test scoring:

- rainfall predictors;
- chronological period boundaries;
- baseline definitions;
- OLS specifications;
- ridge penalty;
- tree and forest settings;
- MAE and RMSE definitions;
- higher-flow threshold;
- treatment of provisional records.

The estimators remain those fitted using 2015–2021 training observations.

Validation data are not added to the fitting sample before the final test.

This conservative choice avoids introducing a new refitting rule after
validation results have already been inspected.[^time-design]

### 15.2 Prepare the Test Table

```{python}
test_predictions = (
    test.copy()
)

if len(
    test_predictions
) == 0:

    raise ValueError(
        "The reserved test sample is empty."
    )

print(
    "Test rows:",
    len(
        test_predictions
    )
)

print(
    "First test date:",
    test_predictions[
        "DATE"
    ].min()
)

print(
    "Last test date:",
    test_predictions[
        "DATE"
    ].max()
)
```

### 15.3 Apply the Three Baselines

```{python}
test_predictions[
    "PRED_MEAN_CFS"
] = training_mean

test_predictions[
    "PRED_MONTH_MEAN_CFS"
] = test_predictions[
    "MONTH"
].map(
    training_month_means
)

test_predictions[
    "PRED_PERSISTENCE_CFS"
] = test_predictions[
    "FLOW_PREV_1D_CFS"
]

if test_predictions[
    [
        "PRED_MEAN_CFS",
        "PRED_MONTH_MEAN_CFS",
        "PRED_PERSISTENCE_CFS"
    ]
].isna().any().any():

    raise ValueError(
        "A test baseline prediction is missing."
    )
```

### 15.4 Apply the OLS Models

```{python}
X_test = (
    test[
        rain_predictors
    ].copy()
)

X_test_simple = (
    X_test[
        [
            "RAIN_PREV_1D_MM"
        ]
    ].copy()
)

X_test_simple = sm.add_constant(
    X_test_simple,
    has_constant="add"
)

X_test_multiple = sm.add_constant(
    X_test,
    has_constant="add"
)

test_predictions[
    "PRED_SIMPLE_OLS_CFS"
] = simple_fit.predict(
    X_test_simple
)

test_predictions[
    "PRED_MULTIPLE_OLS_CFS"
] = multiple_fit.predict(
    X_test_multiple
)
```

### 15.5 Apply Ridge, Tree, and Random Forest

Ridge uses the training-period scaling quantities from Part 13.

```{python}
X_test_scaled = (
    X_test
    - rain_training_means
) / rain_training_scales

test_predictions[
    "PRED_RIDGE_CFS"
] = ridge_model.predict(
    X_test_scaled
)

test_predictions[
    "PRED_TREE_CFS"
] = tree_model.predict(
    X_test
)

test_predictions[
    "PRED_FOREST_CFS"
] = forest_model.predict(
    X_test
)

test_model_columns = list(
    robustness_prediction_columns.values()
)

if test_predictions[
    test_model_columns
].isna().any().any():

    raise ValueError(
        "A final test prediction is missing."
    )
```

### 15.6 Calculate Final Test MAE and RMSE

All methods are scored on the same 723 test dates.

```{python}
final_test_results = pd.DataFrame(
    index=list(
        robustness_prediction_columns
    )
)

final_test_results.index.name = (
    "Method"
)

final_test_results[
    "Test days"
] = len(
    test_predictions
)

for method_name in (
    robustness_prediction_columns
):

    prediction_column = (
        robustness_prediction_columns[
            method_name
        ]
    )

    observed = (
        test_predictions[
            "FLOW_CFS"
        ]
    )

    predicted = (
        test_predictions[
            prediction_column
        ]
    )

    errors = (
        observed
        - predicted
    )

    final_test_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "MAE_cfs"
    ] = errors.abs().mean()

    final_test_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "RMSE_cfs"
    ] = (
        (
            errors ** 2
        ).mean()
        ** 0.5
    )

final_test_results.round(
    3
)
```

### 15.9 Higher-Flow Test Performance

The higher-flow threshold remains the training-period value from Part 14.

It is not recomputed from the test period.

```{python}
test_high_flow_mask = (
    test_predictions[
        "FLOW_CFS"
    ]
    >= high_flow_threshold_cfs
)

test_high_flow = (
    test_predictions.loc[
        test_high_flow_mask
    ].copy()
)

print(
    "Higher-flow test dates:",
    len(
        test_high_flow
    )
)

final_high_flow_results = pd.DataFrame(
    index=list(
        robustness_prediction_columns
    )
)

final_high_flow_results.index.name = (
    "Method"
)

final_high_flow_results[
    "Higher-flow test days"
] = len(
    test_high_flow
)

for method_name in (
    robustness_prediction_columns
):

    prediction_column = (
        robustness_prediction_columns[
            method_name
        ]
    )

    observed = (
        test_high_flow[
            "FLOW_CFS"
        ]
    )

    predicted = (
        test_high_flow[
            prediction_column
        ]
    )

    errors = (
        observed
        - predicted
    )

    final_high_flow_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "MAE_cfs"
    ] = errors.abs().mean()

    final_high_flow_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "RMSE_cfs"
    ] = (
        (
            errors ** 2
        ).mean()
        ** 0.5
    )

final_high_flow_results.round(
    3
)
```

### 15.10 Final Quality-Sensitivity Check

```{python}
test_target_unflagged = (
    test_predictions[
        "PROVISIONAL_FLAG"
    ]
    .eq(
        False
    )
    .fillna(
        False
    )
)

test_previous_unflagged = (
    test_predictions[
        "FLOW_PREV_1D_PROVISIONAL"
    ]
    .eq(
        False
    )
    .fillna(
        False
    )
)

test_quality_mask = (
    test_target_unflagged
    & test_previous_unflagged
)

test_quality_subset = (
    test_predictions.loc[
        test_quality_mask
    ].copy()
)

print(
    "Quality-sensitivity test rows:",
    len(
        test_quality_subset
    )
)

final_quality_results = pd.DataFrame(
    index=list(
        robustness_prediction_columns
    )
)

final_quality_results.index.name = (
    "Method"
)

final_quality_results[
    "Test days"
] = len(
    test_quality_subset
)

for method_name in (
    robustness_prediction_columns
):

    prediction_column = (
        robustness_prediction_columns[
            method_name
        ]
    )

    observed = (
        test_quality_subset[
            "FLOW_CFS"
        ]
    )

    predicted = (
        test_quality_subset[
            prediction_column
        ]
    )

    errors = (
        observed
        - predicted
    )

    final_quality_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "MAE_cfs"
    ] = errors.abs().mean()

    final_quality_results.loc[
        method_name,
        "RMSE_cfs"
    ] = (
        (
            errors ** 2
        ).mean()
        ** 0.5
    )

final_quality_results.round(
    3
)
```

### 15.11 Final Test Findings

The final test contains 723 usable dates from 2024–2025.

Approximate overall test scores are:

| Method | Test MAE (cfs) | Test RMSE (cfs) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Training mean | 4.430 | 5.247 |
| Calendar-month mean | 3.650 | 4.718 |
| Previous-day flow | 1.640 | 3.230 |
| One-day rainfall OLS | 3.603 | 4.384 |
| Three-window rainfall OLS | 3.239 | 4.059 |
| Ridge rainfall | 3.240 | 4.058 |
| Regression tree rainfall | 3.325 | 4.418 |
| Random forest rainfall | 3.249 | 4.274 |

The validation ordering does not transfer perfectly to the final test.

The random forest had the lowest validation errors among the rainfall-only
models.

On the final test, three-window OLS has the lowest rainfall-only MAE,
approximately 3.239 cfs.

Ridge has the lowest rainfall-only RMSE, approximately 4.058 cfs, only
about 0.001 cfs lower than three-window OLS.

Previous-day flow has the lowest overall test MAE and RMSE:

$$
\mathrm{MAE}
\approx
1.640\ \text{cfs},
$$

$$
\mathrm{RMSE}
\approx
3.230\ \text{cfs}.
$$

The final higher-flow subset contains 18 dates.

Approximate higher-flow test MAE is:

| Method | Higher-flow Test MAE (cfs) |
|---|---:|
| Random forest rainfall | 5.885 |
| Regression tree rainfall | 5.994 |
| Three-window rainfall OLS | 6.577 |
| Ridge rainfall | 6.596 |
| One-day rainfall OLS | 6.981 |
| Calendar-month mean | 8.526 |
| Previous-day flow | 8.933 |

Persistence is therefore strongest overall but not strongest on the small
higher-flow test subset.

This distinction shows that a model with the lowest average daily error
need not have the lowest error on unusually high-flow dates.

The quality-status sensitivity test retains 693 of the 723 final-test
dates. On this restricted sample, previous-day flow still has the lowest
overall error, with MAE of approximately 1.561 cfs and RMSE of
approximately 3.142 cfs.

Among the rainfall-only models, three-window OLS and ridge remain nearly
indistinguishable. Their MAE values are approximately 3.221 and 3.223 cfs,
while their RMSE values are approximately 4.013 and 4.012 cfs,
respectively.

The main final-test interpretation therefore does not depend on including
the provisional current-flow or previous-flow observations removed by this
sensitivity rule. This does not prove that all retained unflagged records
are error-free; it only shows that the principal model ranking is stable
under this particular restriction.

```{python}
final_results_dir = Path(
    "Results/Tables"

final_results_dir.mkdir(
    parents=True,

)

final_test_results.to_csv(
    final_results_dir
    / "15_final_test_scores.csv",
    index_label="Method"
)

validation_test_comparison.to_csv(

    / "15_validation_test_comparison.csv",

)

final_high_flow_results.to_csv(

    / "15_final_high_flow_test.csv",
    index_label="Method"

final_quality_results.to_csv(
    final_results_dir
    / "15_final_quality_sensitivity.csv",
    index_label="Method"
```
