```{python}
test_predictions.to_csv(
    final_results_dir
    / "15_final_test_predictions.csv",
    index=False,
    date_format="%Y-%m-%d",
    na_rep=""
)

print(
    "Saved final evaluation results in:",
    final_results_dir
)
```

# Conclusions

## Part 16 — Discussion and Conclusions

### 16.1 Research Question and Scope

This project examines whether historical precipitation at Seattle Sand
Point can support prediction of daily mean streamflow at King County
site 58A.

The study uses previous 1-, 3-, and 7-day precipitation histories and
evaluates several statistical and machine-learning models with chronological
training, validation, and test periods.

The modeled response is daily mean discharge.

It is not an observed flood-event label, instantaneous peak discharge,
or measured inundation extent.

### 16.2 Data Preparation Findings

The Seattle precipitation study period contains 4,018 calendar dates.

After quality screening, 31 dates have unavailable precipitation.

Missing precipitation is not replaced with zero.

The site-58A streamflow calendar also contains 4,018 dates, with 44 missing
daily discharge values.

There are 753 provisional flow records in the source export.

Rainfall-history features are calculated only after restoring the complete
daily calendar.

This prevents missing days from being skipped when defining 1-, 3-, and
7-day rainfall histories.

### 16.3 Rainfall-History Modeling

The one-day rainfall OLS model provides a simple rainfall-only reference.

Adding the previous 3-day and 7-day rainfall totals improves both training
fit and validation prediction.

Three-window OLS has validation MAE of approximately 2.865 cfs, compared
with approximately 3.523 cfs for one-day rainfall OLS.

This indicates that accumulated recent rainfall contains useful predictive
information beyond the immediately preceding day's rainfall.

The cumulative windows overlap, so individual coefficients are not
independent physical runoff effects.

### 16.4 Validation Model Comparison

The validation comparison contains 653 dates from 2022–2023.

Among the rainfall-only candidates, the random forest has the lowest
validation errors:

$$
\mathrm{MAE}
\approx
2.649\ \text{cfs},
$$

$$
\mathrm{RMSE}
\approx
4.151\ \text{cfs}.
$$

Persistence nevertheless has the lowest overall validation MAE:

$$
2.557\ \text{cfs}.
$$

The random forest has the lowest validation RMSE.

No single method is therefore strongest under both development-period
metrics.

### 16.5 Robustness and Higher-Flow Behavior

Restricting validation to dates whose current and previous-day flow records
are both unflagged does not substantially change the main ordering.
The same stability appears in the reserved test period. After restricting
the test sample to 693 dates whose current and previous-day flow records
are both unflagged, persistence still has the lowest overall MAE and RMSE,
while the relative ordering of the main rainfall-only candidates changes
very little.

Persistence remains strongest on overall MAE, while the random forest
remains the strongest tested rainfall-only model on this restricted
validation subset.

The higher-flow comparison gives a different pattern.

Using the training-period 90th percentile, approximately 19.368 cfs, as a
fixed threshold, rainfall-only models outperform persistence on the
higher-flow validation subset.

The same qualitative pattern appears in the higher-flow test subset.

This suggests that previous-day flow is especially effective for typical
daily conditions, while rainfall history may contain relatively more
information during larger flow responses.

However, the higher-flow subsets contain only 40 validation dates and
18 test dates.

They do not provide enough evidence for a strong flood-warning claim.

### 16.6 Final Test Results

The reserved 2024–2025 test contains 723 usable dates.

Previous-day flow has the lowest overall final-test error:

$$
\mathrm{MAE}
\approx
1.640\ \text{cfs},
$$

$$
\mathrm{RMSE}
\approx
3.230\ \text{cfs}.
$$

Among rainfall-only models, three-window OLS has the lowest final-test MAE
at approximately 3.239 cfs.

Ridge has the lowest rainfall-only RMSE at approximately 4.058 cfs, only
about 0.001 cfs below the three-window OLS result.

The random forest had the strongest rainfall-only validation results but
does not retain that advantage on the later test period.

The more flexible model therefore does not generalize uniformly better.

### 16.7 Main Interpretation

The project supports three main conclusions.

First, rainfall history is informative.

Models using previous 1-, 3-, and 7-day precipitation consistently improve
on simple mean-based benchmarks.

Second, recent streamflow is a very strong short-term predictor.

Previous-day-flow persistence has the lowest overall validation MAE and
the lowest overall MAE and RMSE on the final test.

Third, greater model complexity does not guarantee stronger out-of-sample
performance.

The random forest performs best among rainfall-only candidates on
validation, but this advantage does not persist in 2024–2025.

The three-window OLS and ridge models generalize at least as well on the
reserved period.

The higher-flow analysis adds an important qualification.

Rainfall-based models outperform persistence on the selected higher-flow
dates even though persistence is much stronger on average across all days.

### 16.8 Limitations

| Limitation | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Single rainfall station | Sand Point precipitation is a point measurement and may not represent rainfall over the full upstream drainage area. |
| Timing convention | Date labels and historical publication timing do not establish a verified operational forecast lead time. |
| Daily aggregation | Daily mean discharge can smooth short-duration flow peaks. |
| Missing and provisional observations | Complete-case rules change the analyzed sample, and provisional flow records remain in the main fits. |
| Temporal dependence | OLS residuals retain serial dependence, limiting default independent-error inference.[^regression-diagnostics] |
| Validation reuse | Several models were compared repeatedly on the same validation period.[^time-design] |
| Higher-flow sample size | Only 40 validation dates and 18 test dates exceed the fixed higher-flow threshold. |
| Flood definition | Higher daily mean discharge is not identical to an observed flood or inundation event. |

The test period appeared in earlier descriptive inspection of the full
dataset, so it was not completely unseen in every descriptive sense.

However, test prediction errors were not used to select predictors,
hyperparameters, or the higher-flow threshold.

### 16.9 Conclusion

Historical Seattle precipitation contains useful information for predicting
daily mean streamflow at site 58A, particularly when rainfall is summarized
over multiple preceding days.

The project does not show that a more complex rainfall model is always
preferable.

Although the random forest gives the strongest rainfall-only validation
results, that advantage does not persist in the reserved 2024–2025 test.

A simple three-window OLS model performs competitively in the final period,
while previous-day streamflow remains the strongest overall daily
benchmark.

The higher-flow analysis produces a different pattern: rainfall-based
models have smaller errors than persistence on the selected higher-flow
dates.

Together, these results emphasize the importance of chronological
evaluation, strong simple benchmarks, and performance checks beyond one
overall error statistic.

The project should be interpreted as a retrospective daily
streamflow-prediction study rather than an operational flood-warning
system.

:::

```{=html}
<style>
.report-page-nav {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
  margin-top: 2rem;
  padding-top: 1rem;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--bs-border-color, #ddd);
}

.report-page-status {
  flex-basis: 100%;
  text-align: center;
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
}

@media print {
  .report-page-nav {
    display: none !important;
  }
}
</style>

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  const tabset = document.getElementById("report-tabs");

  if (!tabset) return;

  const tabs = tabset.querySelectorAll(
    ":scope > .nav-tabs [role='tab']"
  );

  const pages = tabset.querySelectorAll(
    ":scope > .tab-content > .tab-pane"
  );

  if (
    tabs.length === 0
    || tabs.length !== pages.length
  ) return;

  function openPage(index) {
    tabs[index].click();

    requestAnimationFrame(
      function () {
        tabs[index].focus({
          preventScroll: true
        });

        tabset.scrollIntoView({
          behavior: "auto",
          block: "start"
        });
      }
    );
  }

  for (
    let pageIndex = 0;
    pageIndex < pages.length;
    pageIndex++
  ) {
    if (
      pages[pageIndex].querySelector(
        ".report-page-nav"
      )
    ) continue;

    const nav = document.createElement(
      "nav"
    );

    nav.className =
      "report-page-nav";

    nav.setAttribute(
      "aria-label",
      "Report page navigation"
    );

    const status =
      document.createElement(
        "div"
      );

    status.className =
      "report-page-status";

    status.textContent =
      "Page "
      + (pageIndex + 1)
      + " of "
      + pages.length
      + " — "
      + tabs[
          pageIndex
        ].textContent.trim();

    nav.appendChild(
      status
    );

    function addButton(
      label,
      destination,
      disabled
    ) {
      const button =
        document.createElement(
          "button"
        );

      button.type =
        "button";

      button.className =
        "btn btn-outline-secondary btn-sm";

      button.textContent =
        label;

      button.disabled =
        disabled;

      if (
        destination >= 0
        && destination < tabs.length
      ) {
        button.title =
          tabs[
            destination
          ].textContent.trim();

        button.setAttribute(
          "aria-label",
          label
          + ": "
          + button.title
        );
      }

      if (
        destination === pageIndex
      ) {
        button.className =
          "btn btn-primary btn-sm";

        button.setAttribute(
          "aria-current",
          "page"
        );
      }

      button.addEventListener(
        "click",
        function () {
          openPage(
            destination
          );
        }
      );

      nav.appendChild(
        button
      );
    }

    addButton(
      "← Previous",
      pageIndex - 1,
      pageIndex === 0
    );

    for (
      let index = 0;
      index < pages.length;
      index++
    ) {
      addButton(
        String(
          index + 1
        ),
        index,
        false
      );
    }

    addButton(
      "Next →",
      pageIndex + 1,
      pageIndex
        === pages.length - 1
    );

    pages[
      pageIndex
    ].appendChild(
      nav
    );
  }
});
</script>
```

```{=html}
<style>
.report-sources {
  margin-top: 1.5rem;
}

.report-sources > summary {
  cursor: pointer;
  font-size: 0.95rem;
  padding: 0.6rem 0;
}

.report-sources .footnotes {
  font-size: 0.85rem;
  line-height: 1.5;
}

.report-sources .footnotes > h2 {
  display: none;
}

.report-sources li {
  margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

.report-sources .footnote-back {
  margin-left: 0.3rem;
  white-space: nowrap;
}
</style>

<script>
document.addEventListener(
  "DOMContentLoaded",
  function () {
    const notes =
      document.querySelector(
        "section.footnotes"
      );

    if (
      !notes
      || notes.dataset.deduplicated
         === "true"
    ) return;

    const uniqueSources =
      new Map();

    const sourceById =
      new Map();

    const items =
      Array.from(
        notes.querySelectorAll(
          ":scope > ol > li"
        )
      );

    for (
      const item of items
    ) {
      const copy =
        item.cloneNode(
          true
        );

      copy.querySelectorAll(
        "a.footnote-back"
      ).forEach(
        a => a.remove()
      );

      const text =
        copy.textContent
        .replace(
          /\s+/g,
          " "
        )
        .trim();

      const urls =
        Array.from(
          copy.querySelectorAll(
            "a[href]"
          ),
          a =>
            a.getAttribute(
              "href"
            )
        );

      const key =
        JSON.stringify(
          [
            text,
            urls
          ]
        );

      let source =
        uniqueSources.get(
          key
        );

      if (!source) {
        source = {
          item: item,
          number:
            uniqueSources.size + 1
        };

        uniqueSources.set(
          key,
          source
        );
      }

      sourceById.set(
        item.id,
        source
      );

      if (
        item !== source.item
      ) {
        const paragraph =
          source.item.querySelector(
            "p"
          )
          || source.item;

        for (
          const backlink
          of item.querySelectorAll(
            "a.footnote-back"
          )
        ) {
          paragraph.append(
            " ",
            backlink
          );
        }

        item.remove();
      }
    }

    for (
      const link
      of document.querySelectorAll(
        "a.footnote-ref"
      )
    ) {
      const oldId =
        (
          link.getAttribute(
            "href"
          )
          || ""
        )
        .split(
          "#"
        )
        .pop();

      const source =
        sourceById.get(
          oldId
        );

      if (!source) continue;

      link.setAttribute(
        "href",
        "#"
        + source.item.id
      );

      link.setAttribute(
        "data-footnote-href",
        "#"
        + source.item.id
      );

      link.setAttribute(
        "aria-label",
        "Source "
        + source.number
      );

      const number =
        link.querySelector(
          "sup"
        )
        || link;

      number.textContent =
        source.number;
    }

    for (
      const source
      of uniqueSources.values()
    ) {
      source.item.setAttribute(
        "value",
        source.number
      );

      const backlinks =
        source.item.querySelectorAll(
          "a.footnote-back"
        );

      backlinks.forEach(
        function (
          link,
          index
        ) {
          link.textContent =
            backlinks.length > 1
              ? "\u21A9\uFE0E"
                + (index + 1)
              : "\u21A9\uFE0E";

          link.setAttribute(
            "aria-label",
            "Return to citation "
            + (index + 1)
          );

          link.title =
            "Return to citation "
            + (index + 1);
        }
      );
    }

    let box =
      notes.closest(
        "details"
      );

    if (!box) {
      box =
        document.createElement(
          "details"
        );

      const label =
        document.createElement(
          "summary"
        );

      box.appendChild(
        label
      );

      notes.before(
        box
      );

      box.appendChild(
        notes
      );
    }

    box.classList.add(
      "report-sources"
    );

    box.querySelector(
      "summary"
    ).textContent =
      "Sources and references ("
      + uniqueSources.size
      + ")";

    notes.dataset.deduplicated =
      "true";

    function revealTarget(
      hash
    ) {
      let id;

      try {
        id =
          decodeURIComponent(
            hash.replace(
              /^#/,
              ""
            )
          );
      } catch {
        return;
      }

      const source =
        sourceById.get(
          id
        );

      const target =
        document.getElementById(
          id
        )
        || (
          source
          && source.item
        );

      if (!target) return;

      if (
        notes.contains(
          target
        )
      ) {
        box.open =
          true;
      }

      const panel =
        target.closest(
          ".tab-pane"
        );

      if (panel) {
        const tab =
          document.getElementById(
            panel.getAttribute(
              "aria-labelledby"
            )
          );

        if (
          tab
          && !tab.classList.contains(
            "active"
          )
        ) {
          tab.click();
        }
      }

      requestAnimationFrame(
        function () {
          target.scrollIntoView({
            block: "center"
          });
        }
      );
    }

    document.addEventListener(
      "click",
      function (event) {
        if (
          !(
            event.target
            instanceof Element
          )
        ) return;

        if (
          event.button !== 0
          || event.ctrlKey
          || event.metaKey
          || event.shiftKey
          || event.altKey
        ) return;

        const link =
          event.target.closest(
            "a.footnote-ref, "
            + "a.footnote-back"
          );

        if (link) {
          revealTarget(
            link.getAttribute(
              "href"
            )
            || ""
          );
        }
      },
      true
    );

    window.addEventListener(
      "hashchange",
      function () {
        revealTarget(
          location.hash
        );
      }
    );

    if (
      location.hash
    ) {
      revealTarget(
        location.hash
      );
    }
  }
);
</script>
```

[^noaa-flags]: NOAA NCEI, *GHCN-Daily Documentation*, section II.B and Tables 1–2, https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/cdo/documentation/GHCND_documentation.pdf.

[^pandas-rolling]: pandas documentation, *Series.rolling*, https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.Series.rolling.html.

[^kc-daily-flow]: King County, *Hydrologic Information Center*, description of average daily stream discharge rates, https://green2.kingcounty.gov/hydrology/.

[^pandas-merge]: pandas documentation, *pandas.merge*, https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.merge.html.

[^time-design]: scikit-learn documentation, *TimeSeriesSplit* and *Common pitfalls: data leakage*, https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.model_selection.TimeSeriesSplit.html and https://scikit-learn.org/stable/common_pitfalls.html.

[^simple-baselines]: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, *Forecasting: Principles and Practice*, Section 5.2, mean and naive forecasting methods, https://otexts.com/fpp3/simple-methods.html.

[^baseline-errors]: scikit-learn documentation, *mean_absolute_error* and *root_mean_squared_error*, https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.mean_absolute_error.html and https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.root_mean_squared_error.html.

[^ols-estimation]: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, *Forecasting: Principles and Practice*, Section 7.2, Least squares estimation, https://otexts.com/fpp3/least-squares.html.

[^statsmodels-ols]: statsmodels documentation, *OLS* and *add_constant*, https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/generated/statsmodels.regression.linear_model.OLS.html and https://www.statsmodels.org/stable/generated/statsmodels.tools.tools.add_constant.html.

[^linear-model]: Hyndman and Athanasopoulos, *Forecasting: Principles and Practice*, Section 7.1, The linear model, https://otexts.com/fpp3/regression-intro.html.
